Growing kiwifruit in your home garden

claims.shortExcerpt: Dormant fuzzy kiwifruit is cold hardy to about 0-10°F, while newly developing shoots are frost-sensitive; stage-specific injury is not promoted to whole-plant sensitivity.
Fuzzy kiwifruit is adapted to warmer regions and needs a long frost-free growing season; heat tolerance retained as medium.
Ideal environmental conditions include full sun exposure.
Fertile soil with moderate water-holding capacity is recommended; vines require consistent growing-season moisture.
Kiwifruit vines are sensitive to poor drainage and roots can suffocate in waterlogged soil.
After the winter cold or chilling requirement is satisfied and temperatures warm, buds break; fuzzy kiwifruit has a defined winter dormancy requirement.

claims.value: Reliable bloom requires appropriate winter dormancy/chill and protection of early young growth from spring frost.
claims.shortExcerpt: Kiwifruit break bud early; newly developing young shoots are sensitive to frost injury.

claims.value: Fuzzy kiwifruit needs roughly 225-240 frost-free days, full sun, and compatible pollination for reliable fruit production.
claims.shortExcerpt: Actinidia deliciosa needs about 225 to 240 frost-free days; site selection favors full sun.
